clue.text: Returning star: Bristol runner?

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A star athlete comes home to Bristol after a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords a runner is often a river; the Avon flows through Bristol in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, so the question mark flags a whimsical description of the waterway flowing through that English city.

clue.text: First Lady's partner's an old president

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, and Adam was her mate in Genesis
the possessive ending taken as written

explanation.surface: The husband of a president's wife turns out to be a former president himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' points at a White House wife, but here it means the very first woman, Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth holders of the American presidency.

clue.text: See 5
Flying machine triple echo interfered with

indicators.note: something interfered with has been tampered with and disarranged, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aircraft's radio picks up a threefold echo that disrupts its signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of the two middle words rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary-winged aircraft is a type of airborne craft, so the general description names it fairly.

clue.text: Means to rise to the top in Washington?

definitions.text: Means to rise to the top in Washington?

parts.words: Means to rise to the top in Washington?
parts.note: surface reading: a route to political power in the American capital

parts.words: Means to rise to the top
parts.note: setter's reading: a machine carrying people to the top floor, using the American word for it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like ambition in American politics; Washington just signals the American term for what Britons call a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this word for the cabin that carries people between floors of a building.

clue.text: Move like filthy dogs circling knight in 21 29 18 26

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all round it, so one piece surrounds another
letters that move shift out of their places and settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move like mangy dogs prowling around a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference spells ALFRED LORD TENNYSON CYCLE, so the answer is Tennyson's Arthurian poem cycle, Idylls of the King; the knight sits inside the dogs before everything is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's twelve narrative poems about King Arthur's court form a cycle, which the four cross-referenced answers describe.

clue.text: Subcontract abroad before spring

parts.note: being out means away or abroad
a spring is the source of a stream

explanation.surface: A firm sends work overseas ahead of the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is the place water rises from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean handing work to an outside firm rather than doing it in-house.

clue.text: Kid adopted by the heartless race

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out
being adopted means being taken into a household, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the word with its middle letter dropped
to kid or rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child is taken in by a cold, unfeeling family line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child being adopted, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people or ethnic group is close to a tribe, a community sharing descent.

clue.text: Marrow right when screened by back doctor

indicators.note: something screened is hidden behind a cover, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
the marrow or pith of a matter is its gist
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A spinal specialist checks a patient's bone marrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back doctor' reads as a spine specialist, but the two words split: one is the outer piece, the other the definition. Marrow here is the core of an argument, not the vegetable or bone tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor training beneath consultant level.

clue.text: Fool caught by destiny

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A fool finds himself trapped by fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' looks like a container, but 'by' only means next to, so the cricket abbreviation simply sits beside the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is informal British slang for a stupid person, a mild insult like dope or idiot.

clue.text: Vessel carrying evil weapons

indicators.note: whatever carries a load holds it within, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill can mean evil or harmful, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A ship is transporting sinister arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship carrying weapons, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large guns and cannons, a class of military armament.

clue.text: Hertfordshire town tango band

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A dance band from a small town north of London plays tangos.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London; Tring is a small market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Tring is a market town in the county of Hertfordshire, near the Chiltern Hills in England.

clue.text: Exhausted writer in street

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A worn-out author is wandering the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author, but it is the instrument used for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes something used up or a person with no energy left, matching tired out.

clue.text: Carlos, El Muerto, initially disturbed everyone

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of its proper order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the Spanish word

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed The Dead One unsettles everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: El Muerto looks like a single nickname, but only the first letter of the second word joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: All-comers means anyone at all who wishes to take part, so it covers every person.

clue.text: Receptacle former PM brought in without delay

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece enters another

parts.note: soon means shortly, without much delay
William Pitt (elder and younger) were British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A container is hurriedly carried in for an ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister; the two Pitts led Britain in the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a bowl or vessel provided for people to spit into, so it is a type of container.

clue.text: Dubious plastic recycled outside church

indicators.note: lying outside something means wrapping around it, so one piece surrounds the other
recycled material is broken down and remade in a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether the plastic recycling outside the church really happens.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is a common crossword abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious can describe a person feeling doubt, which is exactly what being doubtful or unconvinced means.

clue.text: Revolutionary film repeatedly inspires a discussion

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run backwards
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien, written out four times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel movie keeps prompting a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The short film title is turned round and laid down four times, with the single letter breathed into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete is a private conversation between two people, literally head to head in French.

clue.text: Legendary ruler in craft endlessly upset

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a craft is a skill or art
upset means hurt; the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A mythical king is distressed while aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat, but it means a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur of Camelot is the mythical British monarch at the heart of the Round Table stories.

clue.text: Dish given author regularly? Controversial matter!

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A writer is served a meal and asks whether it is contentious.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot, as in Lancashire hotpot, is a British baked stew topped with sliced potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a delicate issue too awkward to handle, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Curious new trap set up laureate once

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: curious and nosy both mean inquisitive
N is the abbreviation for new
a net is used to trap animals

explanation.surface: A former poet laureate is caught in an odd new trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym that is part of the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson held the post of Poet Laureate for over forty years in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Score less than 100

parts.note: surface reading: fail to reach a century, as in cricket
setter's reading: a score is twenty, so subtract twenty from a hundred

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as a verb about making runs, but it is the noun for twenty, and the clue is a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred minus twenty, the old counting unit called a score, leaves the number eight tens.

clue.text: Salesman and consumer in Winchester?

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
one who consumes food is an eater

explanation.surface: A salesman and a shopper are found in the cathedral city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the English city, but it is the American rifle maker; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester rifle is a famous lever-action firearm that fires several shots without reloading, an example of that gun type.

clue.text: King Crimson supports a large following

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: The rock band King Crimson is backed by a big fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Crimson' looks like the name of the prog-rock band; in a down clue, the colour supports the rest by sitting beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century Anglo-Saxon monarch, famous for resisting the Vikings.

clue.text: Cover tuna April cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone covers the tuna they cooked in April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like an instruction for the cooked fish, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet used to protect things from rain, a kind of covering.

clue.text: Run with raised speed — run over again!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: pace is speed

explanation.surface: A coach urges a runner to go faster and do the lap again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' appears twice: the first gives a single letter, the second is part of the definition meaning to go over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or go through the main points once more, as when reviewing something already covered.

clue.text: The Dandy's flipping entertaining old satire

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run the other way
to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a dandy is a fop, and the possessive adds S
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: The Dandy, a long-running British children's comic, carries a parody of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make The Dandy look like the British comic, but it is just a fashionable man. 'flipping' also poses as a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a humorous imitation or parody mocking its target, close in sense to satire.

clue.text: Elite soldiers bashing in middle window frame

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, Britain's special forces regiment

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the centre letter of the seven

explanation.surface: Special forces smash their way in through the middle window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bashing in' looks like breaking through, but the second word belongs with 'middle' to pick a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame that holds the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: Offensively smelly G-man keeping it up

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is kept within another

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, called a fed in American slang

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word going up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smelly federal agent keeps up his foul habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping it up' reads as carrying on, but splits into a container signal, a word and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetid describes something giving off a strong, rotten and unpleasant odour, so it is stinking.

clue.text: Revolutionary phase?

parts.note: surface reading: a period of political upheaval
setter's reading: something that goes round and round, a recurring series of events

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests rebellion, but means turning in circles; the answer also ends the cross-referenced title in 5.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a series of events that repeats, coming back round to its start like a revolving wheel.

clue.text: Antagonistic Iran tests explosive

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hostile country carries out weapons tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' sits after the fodder as an adjective, looking like it describes the tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe opposing or pushing back against something, hostile in attitude.

clue.text: One pair in front seeing what's said

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: being in front means leading
the Roman numeral for one
pr is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A single couple sit at the front watching a play.
explanation.walkthrough: PR is a standard abbreviation for pair; 'in front' looks like a phrase, but splits into a container signal and the word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading is understanding speech by watching the speaker's mouth movements, so words are taken in by eye.

clue.text: Devil or demon embracing God

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the run of words holds the answer inside it

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: An evil spirit is wrapped around a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The devil and demon look like the deity's opposites, which suits the surface but they simply supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord is a standard name Christians and Jews use for the deity they worship.
